windows.title: Windows — the Strict Session controller
windows.body: The Windows session manager owns preparation, activation, timer phases, monitoring gates, recovery, and authorized completion. Its native controls require Windows permissions and runtime dependencies.
bullets: Application and browser supervision are platform-specific.
Device signals feed the controller; a heartbeat alone is not a completed monitoring check.
Administration, evidence, points, and session history stay distinct.

android.title: Android — the mobile monitoring companion
android.body: The native Kotlin application combines Android Usage Access, foreground monitoring, permission workflows, routine entry, evidence, and account-scoped local records.
bullets: Accessibility must actually be enabled for its supported enforcement path.
Background operation is subject to Android lifecycle and battery rules.
An extension cannot perform these native phone functions.

ios.title: iOS — camera and screen-sharing sources
ios.body: The checkout contains a secure browser camera companion, Windows reception and health logic, and native screen-sharing reference code. A complete signed, distributed native iOS application is not established here.
bullets: Camera and screen sources have independent role and health tracking.
Windows checks frame arrival, decode, and processing rather than assuming media from a control heartbeat.
Cross-network delivery needs a trusted origin and configured ICE/TURN where required; physical-device validation remains important.

browser.title: Browser — website and media policies
browser.body: The Manifest V3 companion evaluates supported targets and media under browser permissions. Native Windows application control and Android Accessibility remain outside extension scope.
bullets: The installed profile must complete its actual setup and pairing.
Cross-tab decisions, media enforcement, and sensitive-page signaling have implementation paths.
Backend email-prebooking code exists; this does not establish a live mailbox connection.

connectivity.title: Two connections, two responsibilities
connectivity.body: Cloudflare Tunnel or a controlled HTTPS proxy can carry the application gateway and WSS signaling/control channel. It does not itself relay WebRTC video.
bullets: WebRTC attempts a direct negotiated media path where possible.
Authenticated TURN provides a media relay where necessary.
Origin verification, configured credentials, and real reception checks are required before readiness is claimed.

evidence.title: Evidence, approval, and credit are separate facts
evidence.body: The existing submission and receipt workflows retain original files and provenance. An uploaded image, an AI recommendation, a human approval, and a credited ledger event are not interchangeable.
bullets: References resolve to the retained evidence and its checksum.
Authorization and ownership apply when evidence is retrieved.
Incomplete or contradictory records are surfaced without inventing an award.

session.title: Intelligent Session Management
session.body: Strict Session coordinates a persisted lifecycle and policy-defined timer phases through the Windows controller. Readiness, monitoring, pause, recovery, and completion have different meanings.
bullets: Schedules are saved records rather than interface-only timers.
Actual prerequisites and monitoring status control transitions.
Authorized exit and restoration remain part of the lifecycle.

monitoring.title: Coordinated cross-device monitoring
monitoring.body: Windows, Android, the iOS companion, and the browser contribute different signals under their respective permissions. Shared identity connects those events without pretending all clients can perform the same native actions.
bullets: Windows owns the Strict Session lifecycle.
Android supplies native usage and application signals.
Camera, screen, control heartbeat, and receiver health remain independently observable.

camera.title: Camera and screen intelligence
camera.body: The media-health engine compares what the companion says it is producing with what Windows actually receives, decodes, and processes. Each visual source is evaluated independently.
bullets: Sharing disabled, capture interruption, and unknown state are distinct.
Transport, decoder, and processing stalls have distinct diagnostic classifications.
A temporary media gap should preserve session identity while monitoring/study accrual pauses as required.

restriction.title: Application and website restrictions
restriction.body: Access decisions combine the existing policy, supported application or website target, and actual state. Enforcement is provided by the component with the relevant native or browser capability.
bullets: Browser host permissions define its supported website scope.
Android enforcement depends on actual native permission/service state.
Platform availability and policy decisions are not proof that every target has been validated live.

media.title: Application-specific media enforcement
media.body: The centralized media policy distinguishes ordinary restrictions, active rewards, scheduled exceptions, expiry, and unknown state. Continuous playback violations have deduplication paths.
bullets: A SUN NXT exception does not authorize YouTube or Spotify.
Unsupported or uncertain status must not be represented as a verified entitlement.
Essential operating-system audio and emergency paths have separate policy handling.

schedule.title: Scheduled entertainment allowances
schedule.body: The repository contains the specific SUN NXT example: 8:25 PM to 9:35 PM in Asia/Kolkata. It is a target-specific policy window, not a general release of media restrictions.
bullets: The interval begins at 20:25 and closes at 21:35.
An expired window cannot be extended by refreshing the page.
Email-prebooking source is present; public live email integration is not demonstrated by this website.

rewards.title: Verified rewards with a definite expiry
rewards.body: Reward source checks include identity, proof references, timing, eligibility, and expiry. The browser contains authorized YouTube playback and Picture-in-Picture paths; full cross-device operation still depends on runtime service configuration.
bullets: A planned or pending proof is not an awarded entitlement.
Each reward authorizes only its specified target and duration.
Retried requests must not duplicate a reward or point event.

ai.title: Configured AI evidence orchestration
ai.body: The current source includes Taufa primary validation and an official OpenAI API fallback path for technical provider failures. Configuration and actual provider responses are required; this site does not claim a connected live evaluator.
bullets: Original evidence, category, description, and correlation matter.
A provider outage must remain distinguishable from an invalid proof.
Review outcomes, ledger approval, and Demo isolation still follow their own policies. API keys remain server-side.

analytics.title: Reports grounded in retained activity
analytics.body: The reporting code builds summaries from existing activity, submission, evidence, and ledger records. Planned slots, uploaded files, verified tasks, and credited points are separate measures.
bullets: Source event identity and provenance remain available.
Missing authority or reconciliation state must remain explicit.
This public website never fetches personal reports, evidence, or local backend telemetry.

optimization.title: Resource awareness without false readiness
optimization.body: The desktop code has adaptive resource and processing components. Optimizing work is not permission to skip mandatory active-session monitoring or report stale frames as fresh.
bullets: Source-specific freshness and processing remain independent checks.
Lightweight visual effects on this website respect reduced-motion preferences.
No universal CPU, battery, accuracy, or uptime figure is claimed.

faq.question: What is StrictRecords?
faq.answer: An actively developed study discipline and accountability ecosystem, also named StrictRoutines in application builds. It combines routines, focus sessions, device signals, evidence, policy, and a retained record of progress.

faq.question: Which devices are supported?
faq.answer: The repository contains native Windows and Android source, a Chromium Manifest V3 companion, an iOS browser-camera workflow, and native iOS screen-sharing reference code. A complete signed iOS release is not established here. Actual availability depends on the build, device, permissions, and configuration.

faq.question: What controls the Strict Session?
faq.answer: Windows controls the Strict Session lifecycle and timer phases. Device heartbeats and media diagnostics contribute evidence of readiness; they do not independently own or expire the Windows session.

faq.question: How do iOS camera and screen sharing work?
faq.answer: Camera and screen have separate source roles. An authenticated control channel exchanges signaling and status; WebRTC carries visual media, directly or through configured TURN. Windows checks real received, decoded, and processed frames. Native full-screen capture requires the appropriate signed ReplayKit integration and user authorization.

faq.question: What happens when a device disconnects?
faq.answer: The system distinguishes capture, transport, receiver, decoder, processing, and control-channel failures. Recovery aims to retain the Windows session identity; study accrual or monitoring can pause while required signals are unavailable. Physical-device and cross-network checks still matter.

faq.question: How are application restrictions enforced?
faq.answer: Windows uses its native control path, Android uses its available native permissions/services, and the browser extension controls only its supported website scope. No single extension can enforce every native application across all devices.

faq.question: How do scheduled media access and rewards differ?
faq.answer: A scheduled allowance is a specific application window, such as the source's SUN NXT policy at 8:25–9:35 PM Asia/Kolkata. A reward requires its own valid entitlement and expiry. Neither automatically authorizes unrelated media.

faq.question: How is evidence validated?
faq.answer: The current source uses category rules, original evidence, provenance, and configured provider orchestration, including Taufa primary and an official OpenAI fallback path for technical failures. A missing provider is not a successful evaluation. Approval, human review, and point credit remain separate decisions.

faq.question: What data is collected, and what is protected?
faq.answer: Depending on the explicitly enabled workflow, the application can process activity signals, permission/media health, submitted evidence, and session records. Sensitive-page protection is designed to pause visual capture/OCR on detected banking, payment, and personal pages. The public showcase collects no application evidence, uses no analytics tracker, and requests only optional public GitHub metadata. GitHub Pages itself is subject to GitHub's hosting policies.

faq.question: Can I run the whole application on GitHub Pages?
faq.answer: GitHub Pages hosts this static showcase and documentation. Native Windows/Android components, media receivers, authentication, evidence processing, and provider services run in their own configured environments.

faq.question: How can I contribute?
faq.answer: Start with the repository and relevant source/tests, describe a reproducible issue, and propose a focused change. Keep private evidence, credentials, browser state, and generated build output out of commits. Update the maintained website status only with a real source or verification reference.
